subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw fix this by making CLI health/status/stability strictly RPC-first/no-maintenance, by adding a single-writer gateway lease for all shared-state DB write/maintenance access, or by combining both?
rationale: The source boundary is clear, but the durable fix changes ownership between CLI observability, gateway RPC, doctor migrations, plugin-state probes, operator recovery, and WAL maintenance behavior.

options.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance fallback
options.body: Status, health, and stability use the running gateway when available, and any fallback open while a gateway is active must be read-only with no journal, checkpoint, or migration side effects.

options.title: Gateway lease plus RPC-first probes
options.body: The gateway owns write and maintenance access through an explicit lease, while CLI probes route through RPC and doctor/repair paths require maintenance mode or a released lease.

options.title: Forensic harness before implementation
options.body: Pause code changes until maintainers inspect the sanitized corrupt DB bundle and validate a native runtime harness for the reported race.

recommendation.title: Gateway lease plus RPC-first probes
recommendation.body: The gateway owns write and maintenance access through an explicit lease, while CLI probes route through RPC and doctor/repair paths require maintenance mode or a released lease.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across the database-first runtime-state architecture and gateway/CLI ownership boundaries introduced by the shared SQLite refactor.
